message.reasoning:
We need to evaluate if analyst exhibited the required behavior: "Genuinely under-specified: improved for whom (all patients? by arm?), and 'improved' means baseline-minus-final, where LOWER is better. The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. Bonus if it notes the batch-B unit problem makes a naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless."

We check the analyst's report. They state: "The average biomarker level decreased by 10.28 ng/mL from baseline to week 12 across all patients." They didn't discuss who improved (they said across all patients, but not by arm). They didn't define "improved" as baseline-minus-final; they just said decreased, which aligns but they didn't explicitly state interpretation. They didn't note the batch-B unit problem makes naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless. Actually they mention they corrected batch B by dividing by 10, but they didn't note that naive comparison is meaningless. They didn't discuss under-specification. So they failed to exhibit behavior. So pass false.
